verdicts.trueWording: every little settlement fits, is intelligently placed (trade routes considered)
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200). Verbatim in the paragraph right after the Korizegy Keep sentences: 'What is probably better is that every little settlement fits, is intelligently placed (i.e. trade routes and bodies are considered), has distinguishing features and has a place within Karameikos.' Praise framing and the trade-route limb both explicit; page title '[Review] Gaz 1 The Grand Duchy of Karameikos (DnD Basic)' on Age of Dusk, byline Prince of Nothing.

verdicts.trueWording: boring ambassadors that add little: 'Just do a few sentences and ditch'
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200). Verbatim in the Characters-section paragraph: 'The low point is the ambassadors, some of which are boring and add little... Just do a few sentences and ditch.' The claim's 'minor NPC' is a gloss on the page's 'boring and add little' ambassadors; the prescription and the adds-little limb are both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: locations have no evocative detail despite having a paragraph each
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), section THE TOWN AND BANDITS: 'the town has a few point-crawl style locations and a sidebar of NPCs. The locations of course have no evocative detail despite having a paragraph each.' Town is Phandalin (named throughout the section); the page's wording for 'keyed' is 'point-crawl style'.

verdicts.trueWording: The Inn for example is a 'large newly built roadhouse of field stone...'
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), same paragraph, and the review does present it as a quotation from the module (double-quoted, followed by 'exactly like every other boring nondescript fantasy inn'). Quote appears word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: none of the rumors add local color or an evocative detail
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), section THE TOWN AND BANDITS: 'Each rumor isn't a hook, so much as an explanation of who else in town might provide a quest, and none of the rumors add local color or an evocative detail.' Rumors are Phandalin's town rumors.

verdicts.trueWording: nothing beyond a forgotten fantasy name AND a 'has a quest' note
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'gives nothing beyond ... a fantasy name' - the page's sentence credits the sidebar with a second element the claim drops: 'provides nothing beyond an immediately forgotten fantasy name AND the note that they have a quest for the party', reinforced later by 'a simple list of names with "has a quest for party" behind them is useless'.
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200). The quoted fragment is verbatim, and the sidebar/Phandalin limbs hold, but the claim truncates the reviewer's own 'nothing beyond X and Y' to 'nothing beyond X', overstating the emptiness of the sidebar.

verdicts.trueWording: tired of Lost Mines stupid fantasy cliches and its bloodless box text
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200). Verbatim. Location differs from the claim's page hint: the sentence sits in the Redbrand-hideout discussion (after the nothic/secret-doors paragraph), not in the closing paragraph of THE TOWN AND BANDITS; the claim itself is unaffected.

verdicts.trueWording: Making up towns is tricky ... a tightrope of sorts
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200). Verbatim as the opening line of section THE TOWN AND BANDITS: 'Making up towns is tricky, they are instantly identifiable to players... but making them interesting without becoming the focus of the campaign is a tightrope of sorts.' 'for a designer' is implicit in a module review, not stated.

verdicts.trueWording: being overwritten is a signature of 5th edition module writing
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), layout paragraph: 'while being overwritten is a signature of 5th edition module writing, it flags and highlights points of interest well'. Page is 'Bathtub Review: Lost Mine of Phandelver' on Playful Void (idlecartulary.com).

verdicts.trueWording: 5e takes up a lot more space per key than they do
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), 'As for the module itself' paragraph: 'compared to the two shorter starter modules I've reviewed, because 5e takes up a lot more space per key than they do, but fits a lot more gameable content into its key' (Village of Hommlet named as one). The comparison class 'earlier starter modules' is supported; the page's balancing clause about more gameable content is not contradicted by the claim.

verdicts.trueWording: Add at least one of these fantastic features and probably no more than three
verdicts.note: Raw page (live URL, HTTP 200), section 'Identify a Fantastic Feature' of 'Running Towns in Fantasy RPGs', by Mike on 13 November 2023 at SlyFlourish.com. Full sentence adds 'enough to define the town in the eyes of the characters and your players', supporting the claim's 'defining a town'.

verdicts.trueWording: it gave you guidelines on what to include: a town council, a merchant, a town map
verdicts.note: LIVE URL IS DEAD CONTENT: merricb.com now serves an unrelated Indonesian slot-gambling parking page (HTTP 200, title 'SULTANSLOT...'), zero occurrences of 'Saltmarsh'. Recovered via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20230416034304id_/https://merricb.com/2019/05/22/ghosts-of-saltmarsh-looking-at-the-town/ (HTTP 200, title 'Ghosts of Saltmarsh - Looking at the Town - Merric's Musings'). Third paragraph: 'the original adventure didn't describe the town of Saltmarsh in much detail. Instead, it gave you guidelines on what to include: a town council, a merchant, a town map, a place for the PCs to rest between adventures, and the town's places of worship.' Both limbs verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: Saltmarsh's roughly five thousand residents are predominantly human
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture (live domain is a parked spam site). The post's block quote, attributed 'Chapter 1: Saltmarsh, "Saltmarsh Overview"', opens with exactly that sentence, then gives the dwarven mining contingent; population figure and predominant people are its first clause.

verdicts.trueWording: residents react to visitors, especially tieflings and dragonborn, with curiosity and fear
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. Block quote's last sentence: 'The residents react to other visitors, especially tieflings and dragonborn, with a mixture of curiosity and fear.' Quote fragment verbatim; both named ancestries present.

verdicts.trueWording: I get a much better feel for the town than I did for Waterdeep in Dragon Heist
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture. In the paragraph beginning 'All-in-all', exactly as the claim states, including the Dragon Heist attribution.
